title: Universal injectivity into completion from fibre associated primes
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of Noetherian commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal, and let $P$ be a finite $S$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Suppose that for every prime $\mathfrak q\subset S$, with contraction $\mathfrak p\subset R$, if $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}_S(P\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$ then $IS+\mathfrak q\ne S$. Here $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak p)$ is the residue field [def-weil-residue-field], the tensor product has its canonical $S$-action, and associated primes are annihilators of elements as in [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes]. Put $P^\wedge=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}P/I^nP$, the $R$-module of families $x_n\in P/I^nP$ compatible under the quotient maps, with componentwise operations; $I^nP$ is the submodule generated by $ap$ with $a\in I^n$ and $p\in P$. Then the canonical map $u:P\to P^\wedge$, $p\mapsto(p\bmod I^nP)_n$, is universally injective over $R$: for every $R$-module $Q$, $u\otimes_R1_Q:P\otimes_RQ\to P^\wedge\otimes_RQ$ is injective. Tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

proof.text: By [lem-trf-universal-injective-finite-test], it is enough to prove injectivity after tensoring $u$ with each finite $R$-module $Q$; since $R$ is Noetherian, finite modules are finitely presented. Fix such a $Q$.

source.place: Tag 05DM, proof: first paragraph, reduction to a finite R-module Q using Tag 058K

proof.text: There is a canonical map $Q\otimes_R P^\wedge\to (Q\otimes_RP)^\wedge$ induced componentwise by the quotient maps. The composite $Q\otimes_RP\to Q\otimes_RP^\wedge\to(Q\otimes_RP)^\wedge$ is the canonical map to the completion of $M:=Q\otimes_RP$. Therefore injectivity of $M\to M^\wedge$ implies injectivity of $Q\otimes_Ru$.

source.place: Tag 05DM, proof: first paragraph, canonical map to the completion

proof.text: The module $M=Q\otimes_RP$ is finite over $S$ because $Q$ is finite over $R$ and $P$ is finite over $S$. Let $K=\ker(M\to M^\wedge)$. By the definition of the inverse-limit completion, $K=\bigcap_{n\ge1}(IS)^nM$. To prove $K=0$, use [lem-weil-pbc-module-injects-localizations-associated-primes]: it suffices to show $K_{\mathfrak q}=0$ for every $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}_S(M)$.

source.place: Tag 05DM, proof: kernel and associated-prime localization paragraph

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}_S(M)$ and put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$. By [lem-trf-associated-primes-fibre-bound], $\mathfrak q$ is associated to $P\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, so the hypothesis gives $IS+\mathfrak q\ne S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-over-proper-ideal], choose a prime $\mathfrak q\prime\supset IS+\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tag 05DM, proof: associated-prime hypothesis and choice of a prime over IS+q

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-localization] to the Noetherian ring $S$, ideal $IS$, finite $S$-module $M$, and prime $\mathfrak q\prime\supseteq IS$. Its intersection $N=\bigcap_{n\ge0}(IS)^nM$ equals $K$ from Step 3, since the term for $n=0$ is $M$. The cited statement gives $f\in S\setminus\mathfrak q\prime$ with $K_f=0$. Since $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak q\prime$, also $f\notin\mathfrak q$. Thus for any $k\in K$ there is an integer $r\ge0$ with $f^rk=0$, and $k/1=0$ in $K_{\mathfrak q}$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Every fraction in $K_{\mathfrak q}$ is therefore zero.

source.place: Tag 05DM, proof: K_q′ is contained in the intersection of powers and Krull intersection

proof.text: For every $k\in K\subseteq M$ and every $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}_S(M)$, Step 5 shows that $k/1=0$ in $M_{\mathfrak q}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-injects-localizations-associated-primes] to $M$ over the Noetherian ring $S$: it gives $k=0$, hence $K=0$. Step 2 then makes $Q\otimes_Ru$ injective for every finite $Q$, and Step 1 upgrades this to universal injectivity of $u$.

No statement was changed.
